Evidence for the separate reports and presentation

Milestone 4 evaluates the product. The group report, individual report, peer review and presentation are separate submissions with their own criteria. This site supplies evidence for them; it does not replace the required analysis or claim those submissions are complete.

The current official brief asks for reasoned analysis: explain the decision, its motivation, what happened, and what the team learned. Cite a small selection of dated artifacts in an appendix instead of importing the whole site.

Group report — 130 marks

Required section Marks Evidence and analysis starting point
Introduction 10 Purpose and scope · Requirements: explain the product and the report's argument.
Methodology and planning 30 Team process, roadmaps, stakeholder decisions: evaluate how task choice, scope and sequential integration evolved.
Architecture 20 Architecture, API, database, third-party register: assess technology choices, onboarding and trade-offs.
Testing 20 Testing, user feedback, bug tracker: explain how the strategy changed and which feedback produced useful fixes.
Deployment and integration 20 Deployment, Git method, holiday adapter: evaluate CI, hosting, mirror problems and external-service usefulness.
General discussion 20 Release history, known limitations: discuss recurring challenges and future improvements.
Conclusion 5 Synthesise the strongest findings from the analysis.
Supporting documents / appendix 5 Link selected commits, issue records, diagrams and dated evidence from Sources.

Individual report — stated total 100 marks

Required section Printed marks Evidence to select for the author's own contribution
Introduction 10 Personal role and the scope of the reflection.
Responsibilities and contributions 20 Member work records, own branches/PRs and delivered user stories.
Technical challenges and solutions 20 Relevant bug records, failed/successful CI evidence and design trade-offs.
Learning and development 20 Technologies learned, AI use and its effects; AI declaration and technology register.
Collaboration and teamwork 10 Task choice and voting, reviews, integration and communication examples.
General discussion 10 Work the author is proud of, would redo, and the reasons.
Conclusion 10 Personal learning and what would change next time.
Supporting documents / appendix 5 Selected evidence attributable to the author.

Brief arithmetic: section 3.6 prints these eight weights, which add to 105, while its Total row states 100. This guide preserves the published figures rather than silently changing a weighting. The lecturer's interpretation governs marking.

Peer review

Section 3.7 requires a 200–300 word paragraph for each group member, a rating from 0 to 5, and a self-rating. Describe observed contributions with specific examples. The personal evaluation and anonymous peer review are submitted separately; no peer ratings are invented or published here. See the official instructions.

Group presentation — 110 marks

Criterion Marks Useful material
Product showcase 40 Product overview, selected real role journeys, interface and recovery states.
Technical breakdown 20 Architecture, diagrams, one complete UI → API → database flow.
Presentation quality 40 Clear structure, timing, project coverage, visual aids and shared delivery.
Questions 10 Explain choices, limits and code behaviour; involve the relevant team members.

A demonstration should distinguish a design mockup, recorded evidence and a working live feature. Official presentation rubric.
